name: Hilkiah
overview: Hilkiah was a male Levite who served as an Aaronic priest through the lineage of Eleazar. He is identified as the son of Shallum and father of Azariah, and notably stood at Ezra's right hand during the public reading of the Law, indicating a significant priestly role in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Hilkiah means 'YHWH is [my] portion,' reflecting a personal dedication to the Lord. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:13 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a theologically rich meaning consistent with his priestly service.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hilkiah as the son of Shallum and the father of Azariah (1 Chronicles 6:13). Additionally, inferred relationships include being the father of Hashabiah (Nehemiah 12:21) and Gemariah (Jeremiah 29:3), situating him within a notable priestly lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Hilkiah's significance lies in his role as a Levite and Aaronic priest who actively participated in the religious reforms and restoration of worship practices, as evidenced by his presence alongside Ezra during the Law's public reading. His priestly lineage through Eleazar underscores his legitimate service in the temple, and his familial connections highlight his place within the continuity of Israel's priesthood.
